name: Phase-pipeline turn loop
what: Each model iteration runs a fixed sequence of small phase modules; a phase returns break/continue/return and the thin outer loop obeys it, so a change to overflow, recovery or truncation touches one file.
how: conversation_loop._run_conversation_turn loops while (api_call_count < max_iterations and iteration_budget.remaining > 0) or a grace call is armed, calling _run_phase over begin_iteration, prepare_iteration, assemble_api_request, run_preflight_gate, announce_api_call, a retry loop, normalize_model_response, then run_tool_round or finish_text_response; finalize_turn runs after the loop. About 33 turn_*.py siblings own one phase each. The loop is synchronous Python on threads with interrupt checks between phases.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's plain-chat loop is one ~3,700-line function (model-gateway sse.rs invoke_stream_sse) and Do mode is a 13.5k-line agent.rs; a phase table with an enforced per-unit complexity ratchet is a concrete way to decompose both.
notes: Quality 4 because the decomposition is enforced by a CI ratchet (CC 20, 300 lines per function, 2,000 per file, units already over may only shrink). Weakness: Python threads and the GIL, no async cancellation primitives; the Rust port would use tasks.

name: Unbounded-by-default iteration budget with grace call and wall-clock budget
what: A turn has no default iteration cap because caps caused silent mid-task truncation; an optional finite cap gets a one-turn grace call, an optional warning ratio, and an optional wall-clock run budget with a wrap-up notice at 80 percent.
how: IterationBudget is a locked consume/refund counter; execute_code iterations are refunded so programmatic tool calls do not spend it. AIAgent max_iterations defaults to sys.maxsize and agent.max_turns defaults to None; agent.run_budget_seconds adds the wall-clock budget and caps implicit provider stale timeouts. Each subagent holds its own budget (delegation.max_iterations 250).
verevonRelevance: Verevon caps both loops at 12 rounds (ceiling 32); Hermes treats a low cap as a truncation bug and relies on guardrails plus a time budget instead, which is the better default for long agentic work.
notes: Doc-vs-code discrepancy: agent/AGENTS.md:16 and iteration_budget.py:5 still say the default is 500 (subagents 50); the code default is unlimited and delegation.max_iterations is 250. Code is ground truth.

name: Provider error taxonomy with recovery hints
what: Every API failure is classified into one of about 30 failover reasons that carry explicit recovery flags (retry, compress, rotate credential, fallback), so the retry loop never re-matches error strings itself.
how: agent/error_classifier.py defines the FailoverReason enum (auth, billing, rate_limit, upstream_blocked, overloaded, context_overflow, image_too_large, content_policy_blocked, model_entitlement, thinking_signature, role_alternation, and more) and ClassifiedError with retryable/should_compress/should_rotate_credential/should_fallback. Plugins may override via the transform_api_error_classification hook and each ProviderProfile may supply classify_api_error; both run before the built-in priority pipeline.
verevonRelevance: inference-core types overflow and retries transient failures but has no equivalent single vocabulary tying failure class to recovery action across Azure, Anthropic, Cohere and the Codex route; adopting one enum shared by both loops would remove duplicated retry logic.
notes: Many patterns are substring tables tuned to specific vendor wording (OpenRouter, Anthropic OAuth, Nous), so they rot as vendors change text; structured error codes are preferred where available.

name: Post-exhaustion auto-recovery ladder
what: When retries and the fallback chain are spent on a transient provider outage, the turn parks with a visible countdown and retries up to five more cycles instead of failing, but only if no answer text has been delivered.
how: turn_recovery_autorecover.py engages for overloaded, server_error and timeout verdicts only; jittered 15/30/60/60/60 s waits, a provider Retry-After wins up to 120 s; the wait is interruptible and the notice names the stop gesture per surface (Esc on CLI/TUI/desktop, cancel request on API, /stop on chat). Config agent.auto_recovery_cycles defaults to 5.
verevonRelevance: A chat product on shared infrastructure sees provider brownouts; a visible, bounded, interruptible wait that never replays delivered text is a small change with large perceived-reliability gain for Verevon's streaming path.
notes: Only transient classes enter; auth, billing, policy and format errors never do, which keeps the ladder from masking real faults.

name: Failed-turn boundary closure keeps the transcript well-formed
what: When a turn dies without a final answer, the loop appends a system-authored assistant row so the stored conversation never ends on an open user message that would be merged into the next prompt.
how: _close_durable_failed_turn writes an assistant row with display_kind FAILED_TURN and force-redacted error metadata (error_surface) into result messages and SessionDB, idempotent on the durable tail role; context-pressure failures (compression_exhausted, context_overflow) are excluded to avoid a growth loop.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's session-core is the single writer for runs and events; a rule that every failed run leaves a typed, redacted terminal row (rather than 'finalization_pending' only) would make resume and rewind semantics simpler on the chat page.
notes: The error text is redacted with force=True even when security.redact_secrets is off, because it lands in a durable store that is later exported.

name: Stop gates that turn a text answer into another iteration
what: When the model stops with prose after editing code, up to three gates can append the answer as an interim row plus a synthetic nudge and continue the turn: verify-on-stop, a pre_verify plugin hook, and a kanban terminal-tool guard.
how: turn_stop_gates.apply_stop_gates runs the three gates in order, flags the nudge as a user-role synthetic row only after the assistant row (alternation preserved), keeps the candidate answer as a budget-exhaustion fallback and sets finish_reason verification_required / verify_hook_continue / kanban_terminal_required. Bounded by agent.max_verify_nudges.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has deterministic post-condition verifiers for provider writes; the stop-gate shape lets those verifiers push the loop forward in-band instead of only labelling the result.
notes: The pre_verify hook accepts the Claude Code Stop decision shape, so existing hook scripts port over.

name: Tool-loop guardrails: repeat, cycle and no-progress detection
what: A side-effect-free controller detects identical failing calls, same-tool failure streaks, idempotent no-progress, and repeating A,B,A,B call cycles, warns first, and hard-stops by default only on unattended surfaces.
how: tool_guardrails.py holds IDEMPOTENT/MUTATING/FAILURE_TOLERANT/PROGRESS_RESET tool sets, thresholds (warn after 2/3/2, halt after 5/8/5), cycle detection up to period 4 over a 64-call history, byte-identical result stubbing from the second repeat above 512 chars, and per-turn caps (50 web searches, 50 subagents). Interactive platforms (cli, tui, desktop, acp, subagent, api_server) are warn-only; gateway and cron hard-stop.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has retry and round budgets but no repeat/cycle detector; this controller is a pure function that the Rust loops could host unchanged and it protects scheduled runs where nobody can press stop.
notes: The cycle detector is a port of an oh-my-pi fix, a sign of cross-harness borrowing. Hard stop is opt-in on interactive surfaces so legitimate edit-test loops are not cut.

name: Path-scoped parallel tool-batch planner
what: A model batch of tool calls is split into ordered parallel and sequential segments so read-only calls run concurrently while a writer never overlaps any reader or writer of the same path.
how: _plan_tool_batch_segments admits calls via _batch_admission: never-parallel interactive tools are barriers, a fixed safe set (read_file, search_files, web_search, web_extract, vision_analyze, image_generate, session_search, skill_view) runs in parallel, read_file/search_files/write_file/patch are admitted by canonical-path overlap (readers may share a subtree, any overlap with a writer closes the run), MCP tools opt in via supports_parallel_tool_calls. Result order always equals call order; runs shorter than two demote to sequential.
verevonRelevance: Both Verevon loops use join_all over the whole round with no conflict analysis; a path-reservation planner would make parallel dispatch safe for file and workspace tools and keeps results ordered for replay.
notes: Overlap uses realpath plus normcase so symlinks and Windows case do not defeat it; unknown scope is treated as a barrier (fail closed).

name: Concurrent executor with start-order and approval-serialization gates
what: Concurrent tool workers start in call order, approval prompts are serialized so they never interleave on screen, and time a human spent approving is excluded from the batch deadline.
how: execute_tool_calls_concurrent uses a DaemonThreadPoolExecutor (max 8 workers), a _StartOrderGate that releases workers in submit order and can be abandoned, and _ConcurrentToolAuthorizationGate that serializes policy prompts with a bounded acquire and measures human-wait at its source so a wedged plugin cannot extend the deadline. Results are appended in original order; a batch timeout synthesizes results for unfinished calls.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's HITL approvals are durable and out-of-band, so interleaving is less of a problem, but the idea of excluding human wait time from tool deadlines applies directly to its wall-clock budget (EXECUTION_RUN_WALL_CLOCK_SECS).
notes: Every gate has a bounded wait that falls back to 'proceed out of order' rather than starve the batch, each tied to a numbered incident in comments.

name: Agent-level inline tools and layered tool-execution pipeline
what: Tools that need agent state (todo, memory, delegation helpers) are intercepted by a table before the registry, and every tool call passes the same observe, guard, middleware, execute, commit pipeline on both the sequential and concurrent paths.
how: INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS maps tool names to handlers with an InlineToolContext; adding one means adding a table entry, never an if-chain. The pipeline resolves tool_search bridge calls to the real tool name, runs pre_tool_call block/modify hooks, guardrails, approval, tool_request/tool_execution middleware, then _commit_tool_result persists, redacts, spills large output and emits events.
verevonRelevance: A single execution funnel for both of Verevon's loops would close the gap where hooks are not applied in Do mode (hook_context is empty) and MCP calls are denied for lack of a binding.
notes: The rule 'table, not if-chain' is repeated for slash commands, RPC methods and backends, a consistent house style.

name: Interrupt categories and mid-turn steer, queue and redirect
what: A busy session can be interrupted, steered (text injected after the next tool result), queued or redirected according to display.busy_input_mode, and the loop records whether a stop came from a human or a system watchdog.
how: interrupt_control.py separates user reasons (explicit stop, new message, user interrupt) from system tool_reason values (watchdogs, lease loss); /steer is delivered as a standalone user row after a tool result so assistant(tool_calls) to tool to user stays legal on every provider; a steer arriving after the final assistant turn is returned as pending_steer and becomes the next user turn. A rewind submit is never absorbed by busy-input policy and returns code 4009 while busy.
verevonRelevance: Verevon supports mid-run input and cancel in chat; attributing stops to a producer (user vs lease vs watchdog) and delivering steer as a standalone row are directly reusable for its run-event model.
notes: Steer never mutates the persisted tool row, because append-only persistence would then diverge from the live request.

name: Two-layer context compaction with provider-anchored token accounting
what: A gateway-side hygiene pass fires at 85 percent of the window as a safety net, while the in-loop compressor fires at 50 percent (floored at 75 percent for windows under 512K) using the provider's real token counts plus a rough estimate of only the new messages.
how: gateway/run_turn session hygiene uses last API-reported tokens, then a usage anchor persisted on the session row (content-fingerprinted so it survives history reloads and restarts), then a character estimate; agent ContextCompressor runs at turn start, idle, pre-API and post-tool gates. compression.threshold, threshold_tokens, per-model overrides (longest substring wins), tail_mode lean/legacy, max_attempts are config.
verevonRelevance: Verevon compacts in two tiers (clear stale tool results, then summarize head) with a reattach_context tool; the anchor-based accounting and a fixed safety-net layer below the main trigger are cheap additions that avoid premature compaction on long chat sessions.
notes: Intermediate 'context pressure' warnings were removed because they made models give up early on hard tasks (turn_iteration_prep note).

name: Prune-first structured-summary compression with iterative re-compression
what: Compression first clears old tool results with no LLM call, then summarizes only the middle into a fixed structured template, and later compactions update the previous summary instead of re-summarizing.
how: Phase 1 replaces tool results over 200 chars outside the protected tail with a placeholder; phase 2 aligns boundaries so tool_call/tool_result groups stay together and sizes the tail by token budget (at most 20 percent of the window); phase 3 calls the auxiliary compression model with a Goal/Constraints/Progress/Decisions/Files/Next/Critical template (budget 20 percent of content, 2K to 12K tokens); phase 4 assembles head, summary marker (role chosen to keep alternation) and tail and repairs orphan tool pairs. User messages are carried verbatim in lean tail mode.
verevonRelevance: Mirrors Verevon's tier 1 and tier 2; the useful extras are the structured template, the token-budgeted tail with atomic tool groups, and keeping the previous summary as the base for updates.
notes: The doc warns the summary model must have at least the main model's context window or the middle is dropped without a summary; evals/compaction scores policies by recall of gold questions, not token savings.

name: Compression failure cooldown, provider-proven overflow and deterministic fallback
what: A failed or stalled summary attempt arms an escalating per-session cooldown persisted in the database, and a repeated stall ends in a deterministic static summary committed through the normal pipeline rather than a skipped compaction.
how: Cooldown ladder 60 s, 300 s, 900 s (never shorter than compression.context_timeout_seconds), separate counter for summaries that hit finish_reason length, flat 30 s for decode errors; manual /compress and same-turn fallback_chain retries bypass it; context limits learned from provider overflow errors persist (Bedrock cache with provenance map and five-minute failed-probe cooldown).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's compaction retry on prompt-too-long has no persisted failure state; persisting a cooldown on the session row prevents the loop where a broken summary route re-fires every turn.
notes: Read from the developer guide and AGENTS; the escalation constants were not re-verified in code line by line.

name: Opt-in micro-compaction that never compacts user messages
what: An optional mode folds the single oldest exchange into a running summary after every turn, paying compression in small instalments, while user messages stay verbatim for the whole session.
how: MicroCompactionMixin on ContextCompressor absorbs one assistant-led exchange per turn (compression.micro_compact, off by default), rehydrates the rolling summary from the surviving marker after resume, and the doc states the cost: each pass rewrites the cached prefix.
verevonRelevance: The never-compact-user-text rule is a principled constraint Verevon can adopt for its own compaction tiers; the amortized mode itself conflicts with prompt-cache economics and is correctly default-off.
notes: Hermes states the tradeoff plainly in the docs, a transparency habit worth copying.

name: Native provider compaction handed first shot, local compressor as fallback
what: On OpenAI Responses routes that support server-side compaction the provider gets the first chance to compact, clamped just below the local trigger, and the local compressor only fires if native did not.
how: native_compaction.py sends context_management compaction with a threshold 8,192 tokens below the local trigger for gpt-5.6 and gpt-6-astra on official routes; compaction items ride the codex_reasoning_items sidecar; a separate codex_app_server_auto setting (native|hermes|off) governs thread compaction when Codex owns the loop.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon keeps the user's-ChatGPT-subscription route through the Codex app-server, an explicit two-owner compaction handoff avoids two systems racing on the same context.
notes: Narrow eligibility by design; opaque compaction items cannot be inspected or edited, a transparency cost.

name: Per-conversation prompt-cache invariant governs all mid-conversation injection
what: The system prompt is byte-stable for the life of a conversation; anything that must change mid-session rides a user message or tool result, and slash commands that alter prompt state defer to the next session unless the user passes --now.
how: Root rule plus agent rules: skill slash commands inject as user messages, subdirectory AGENTS.md hints append to tool results (32K cap), /steer is a standalone row, surface switches (desktop to TUI) send a one-shot note instead of rewriting the stored platform line, the skills index delta rides the same note channel, and compression is the only sanctioned cache break.
verevonRelevance: Verevon computes custom-instruction hierarchy and memory per turn; making cache-stability a named review invariant, with tests that assert byte-stable prefixes, would protect cost on the Anthropic and Azure routes.
notes: Model or credential switches also reset provider caches; docs for /model, fallback and credential pools carry explicit cost warnings and the code refuses to swap silently.

name: Three-tier system prompt ordered for prefix-cache reuse
what: The system prompt is assembled as stable, context, then volatile tiers, with project files placed before any worktree-specific line so sessions of one project in different worktrees share the longest cached prefix.
how: agent/system_prompt.py assembles stable (identity or SOUL.md, tool and model guidance), context (system_message, .hermes.md/AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules, git workspace snapshot, operator and platform hints), volatile (skills index, MEMORY and USER snapshots, external memory block, timestamp/model line, runtime environment ending the prompt). platform_hints in config can append or replace a hint per platform inside the stable tier.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's platform to org to Space to agent to persona instruction stack could be ordered the same way (stable first, per-run volatile last) to keep the cached prefix long.
notes: Context-file loading accepts other tools' rule files (CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules), a deliberate interoperability choice.

name: Large tool-result spillover with per-turn budget
what: Tool output over a per-tool threshold is written to disk and replaced by a short preview and path, with MCP results held to a tighter cap and a whole-turn budget enforced on top.
how: maybe_persist_tool_result persists over 100K chars (50K for mcp_ tools) to HERMES_HOME/cache/spillover with a 1,500-char preview inside persisted-output tags; read_file is pinned to infinity to avoid persist-read loops; enforce_turn_budget caps total result size per turn (200K); remote backends get a translated in-sandbox path.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already turns large results into queryable handles (result_query); Hermes adds the per-turn total budget and the pinned-exception for the read tool, both missing safeguards.
notes: Delegation results use a parallel mechanism (max_summary_chars 24,000 with spill to cache/delegation and a read_file footer).

name: Programmatic tool calling with session-persistent Python kernels
what: The model writes a Python script that calls a whitelist of Hermes tools over RPC, collapsing multi-step chains into one inference turn, and variables persist across calls in a per-conversation kernel.
how: execute_code runs in a kernel keyed by (owner, mode, interpreter, cwd, tool-set) over a Unix socket (loopback TCP on Windows) with a per-kernel random frame sentinel, env scrubbing, per-cell tool budget (default 50) and RPC token; allowed tools are web_search, web_extract, read_file, write_file, search_files, patch, terminal; kernels die on timeout, after 1,800 s idle or by LRU past 4; remote backends use a request-file poll fallback; iterations are refunded to the budget.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's baseline lists 'code mode (tools callable from the sandbox)' as absent and code_interpreter has the network disabled; this is a ready design for a tool-RPC bridge with token, budget and env scrubbing.
notes: A timed-out cell kills the kernel because a cell cannot be interrupted safely in place; state loss is deliberate.

name: Background process registry with notify, watch and heartbeat events
what: Long-running commands run in the background with a rolling output buffer, poll/log/wait/kill, completion notifications that start a new turn, optional pattern watches, and periodic heartbeat events.
how: process_registry.py keeps a 200KB rolling buffer, JSON checkpoint for crash recovery, notify_on_complete, watch_patterns (disabled after repeated deliveries and degraded to notify_on_complete), heartbeat_seconds served by one daemon timer for all sessions; teardown SIGTERMs the recorded parent first, waits terminal.daemon_term_grace_seconds, then the snapshotted descendants, then SIGKILL; delegated children can hand a process to the parent via process_manage handoff.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Space-scoped process_start/read/stdin/signal under bwrap lacks completion-triggered turns and parent-first teardown ordering.
notes: Parent-first signalling exists because killing a Chromium zygote first turns exit 0 into a core dump (documented incident).

name: Subagent delegation with leaf and orchestrator roles, batches and output schemas
what: delegate_task spawns children with isolated context and terminal; single or batch (concurrency-capped), leaf or orchestrator roles, optional output_schema validation, group-joined background completions, and a stop that fans out to background units.
how: delegation config: max_concurrent_children 10, max_spawn_depth 1 (flat; 2 enables orchestrator to leaf), orchestrator_enabled kill switch, child_timeout_seconds 0 (inactivity-based, not wall clock), inherit_mcp_toolsets, max_summary_chars 24,000; leaf children lose delegate_task, clarify, memory, send_message, cronjob, start_chat; an output_schema miss after one retry keeps status completed with schema_valid false; child kernels and background processes are disposed or handed off at teardown.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's subagent.task is depth 1, up to 8 children and requires consent to read results back; the child-result handling (never discard a result on schema miss, inactivity timeouts) is worth copying.
notes: Doc-vs-code discrepancy: tools/AGENTS.md says defaults 3 children and depth 2; config_defaults.py sets 10 and 1. The earlier Verevon analysis already covered the leaf/orchestrator split.

name: Durable async-delegation ledger with honest unknown outcomes
what: Background delegations are executed on threads in the owning process but recorded in the state database, so after a crash the parent receives an explicit outcome-unknown completion with transcript tails and a git-state hint instead of silence or a fake result.
how: async_delegation persists dispatch and completion rows (owner pid and start time), recover_abandoned_delegations classifies dead-owner rows as unknown and replays child results already recorded, completions are claimed with delivery states (claim/release/defer/complete) and enqueued as new turns, never mid-turn.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Temporal workflows give durable execution; the transferable part is the explicit 'unknown' terminal state with diagnostics and the claim-based at-least-once delivery of completions to the chat.
notes: tools/AGENTS.md:144 still says background delegation is process-local; execution is, but the ledger is durable. Execution does not resume after a crash.

name: Public subagent lifecycle API with capability handles
what: Plugins launch and supervise child sessions through a service with serializable, unforgeable handles and a fixed state machine, without importing delegation internals.
how: ctx.subagent_lifecycle exposes launch, status, wait, cancel, steer, result, reconnect; states PENDING to CANCELLED plus UNKNOWN; cancel is cooperative; results are immutable, bounded to 32K chars, omit transcripts and carry a stable hash; requests are fail-closed (parent-broadening toolsets rejected); metadata kept in process for one hour, reconnect after restart returns RECONNECT_UNAVAILABLE.
verevonRelevance: A typed lifecycle contract for child runs (status, steer, cancel, hash-stamped result) would give Verevon's agent page a stable API to render sub-agent trees from without reaching into execution-core.
notes: The TUI/desktop snapshot adds subagent.list/tail/steer/interrupt with exact-generation authority so a reattached client cannot control a foreign child.

name: Opt-in subagent git worktrees and cross-agent file-state registry
what: Children can work in their own git worktree and branch, and a process-wide registry stops one agent overwriting a file another agent changed after it was read.
how: subagent_worktree.py creates <repo>/.worktrees/subagent-<id> on branch hermes-subagent/<id>, local backend only, pruned only when proven clean with zero commits; file_state.FileStateRegistry records per-agent read stamps and the last writer with a per-path lock, and write_file refuses a stale or never-read whole-file overwrite (HERMES_DISABLE_FILE_STATE_GUARD turns it into a warning).
verevonRelevance: Verevon rejected worktree isolation in its ledger; the file-state guard is the cheaper half and applies to any shared Space workspace with concurrent sub-runs.
notes: Worktree isolation is skipped on docker/ssh/modal because the host worktree is invisible in the sandbox.

name: Transparent filesystem checkpoints in one shared shadow git store
what: Before file-mutating tools run, the working directory is snapshotted once per turn into a shared shadow repository so any change can be rolled back, without the model ever seeing a tool for it.
how: checkpoint_manager.py uses GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_INDEX_FILE against ~/.hermes/checkpoints/store with refs/hermes/<hash16> per project so objects deduplicate across worktrees; config checkpoints.enabled (default false), max_snapshots 20, max_total_size_mb 500, auto_prune with 7-day retention that never deletes orphans automatically; /rollback and hermes checkpoints expose it; tool_executor calls _ensure_file_checkpoint before writes.
verevonRelevance: For Spaces that edit documents or files, a deduplicated snapshot-before-write with bounded retention is a cheap undo layer beneath the existing Proof Bundle.
notes: Disabled by default, so most users never benefit; a fix in v2 moved from per-project shadow repos (about 40 MB each) to the shared store.

name: Post-turn background review fork that writes memory and skills
what: After a turn is delivered, a daemon thread forks the agent on a snapshot of the conversation and asks whether any memory or skill should be saved, without touching the live conversation or its prompt cache.
how: background_review.py forks AIAgent inheriting provider, credentials and the cached system prompt (same prefix cache), runs under a dispatch-side tool whitelist (skill and memory tools plus read-only file tools) set per thread, with per-run cancellation tokens that a new live turn can supersede. Triggers: memory nudge every 10 user turns, skill review after 10 tool iterations (memory.nudge_interval, skills.creation_nudge_interval). Review prompts enforce class-level umbrella skills, read-before-write via skill_view, and a do-not-capture list.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's session-core Dreaming and SkillPromotion workflows serve the same goal; the transferable pieces are the cache-sharing fork, the dispatch-side whitelist, and the supersede-on-new-turn cancellation.
notes: The fork costs about 30K tokens per event (code comment) and is suppressed for cron. The earlier Verevon analysis noted it ran unmetered; no eval of whether learned skills improve outcomes exists in the tree.

name: Idle-triggered skill curator that archives, never deletes
what: A background maintenance pass tracks skill usage and, when the agent is idle and the last run is old enough, moves stale agent-created skills to a restorable archive, with optional LLM consolidation.
how: agent/curator.py: interval_hours default 168, min_idle_hours 2, stale after 14 days, archive after 30, state in skills/.curator_state, usage telemetry in .usage.json (use/view/patch counts, state, pinned); touches only created_by agent skills, pinned skills exempt, LLM consolidation off by default, pre-run tar.gz backups and rollback via hermes curator.
verevonRelevance: A reversibility envelope (snapshot, archive-only, pin exemption, dry-run) is the right shape for any Verevon autonomous library curation such as SkillPromotion.
notes: Already covered in the earlier Verevon docs; listed here for the concrete defaults and invariants.

name: Cron scheduler with at-most-once slots, catch-up windows and inactivity watchdog
what: Scheduled jobs are full agent runs with skills, scripts, chained context, per-job model and workdir, and delivery to any platform; the scheduler accounts for every occurrence and cannot double-fire or silently drop one.
how: cron/jobs.py and scheduler.py: tick advances next_run_at before dispatch and stamps pending_slot in the same save; a dead owner's slot is restored once (occurrences.py) and an executions ledger blocks a second fire; catch-up window is half the period clamped to 2 minutes to 2 hours; inactivity (not wall-clock) watchdog defaults to 600 s; per-home tick lock; pre-run script output injected into the prompt, no_agent mode, context_from chaining, workdir loads that directory's AGENTS.md.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's scheduled run is a single no-tool 1,024-token call with no delivery; adopt the occurrence accounting, inactivity watchdog, script-injection and context_from chaining before building richer scheduled agents.
notes: Unattended cron sessions default to hard-stop guardrails and approvals.cron_mode deny.

name: Multi-profile cron ticker and Chronos managed one-shot cron
what: One host process ticks every served profile's store under that profile's secret scope, and a hosted variant arms one external one-shot per job so an idle gateway can scale to zero.
how: scheduler_provider._start_multiplex iterates profiles_to_serve sequentially under _profile_cron_scope; in-flight state is keyed by (home key, job id) and pools reaped when a home leaves; the Chronos provider calls NAS provision endpoints, NAS arms a one-shot at the real next fire time and calls back POST /api/cron/fire with a short-lived JWT (purpose cron_fire), and the agent re-arms the next one.
verevonRelevance: Scale-to-zero scheduling by external one-shot arming is a pattern Verevon's Temporal cron could use for idle tenants instead of polling sweepers.
notes: The 'per-profile process assumption is the bug class' lessons (claims released under the registering key, state keyed by home) apply to any multi-tenant scheduler.

name: Kanban multi-agent work queue with dispatcher, swarm and PR acceptance
what: A durable SQLite board lets several profiles collaborate: cards with dependencies are claimed atomically and run as separate worker sessions that must finish with a terminal board tool, with review gates and optional exact-head GitHub PR acceptance.
how: hermes_cli/kanban*.py plus kanban_* tools (show, complete, block, request_review, request_changes, create, link, attach, heartbeat); dispatcher (default 60 s, in the gateway) reclaims stale claims, promotes ready tasks, spawns assigned profiles with HERMES_KANBAN_TASK/DB/BOARD pinned in a scrubbed env, respawn circuit breaker (failure_limit 2, terminal provider exit code 78), worker liveness by (pid, start time); board is the hard isolation boundary, tenant a soft namespace; swarm topology = planning root, parallel specialists, verifier, synthesizer with a JSON blackboard in comments.
verevonRelevance: Missed by the earlier Verevon analyses; maps to Verevon's tasks and WideResearch/DeepTask workflows and shows a worker-lane contract and respawn breaker that a task board on the agent page would need.
notes: Lane identity is an assignee string; tasks with unresolvable assignees stay ready with a skipped_nonspawnable event rather than falling back.

name: Persistent goals, loops and heartbeats driven as plain user messages
what: /goal keeps an objective alive across turns judged by an auxiliary model with optional completion contract and deterministic quality gates; /loop and /heartbeat re-enter a session on a schedule; all inject ordinary user messages so prompt caching stays intact.
how: hermes_cli/goals.py: default 20 turns, judge fail-open (continue) with auto-pause after 3 parse failures or 5 transport failures, gates are shell commands that must pass before the judge may declare done and whose output becomes the next prompt, wait barriers up to 30 min; loops.py stops on LOOP_COMPLETE, --times, an --until judge or max_ticks 100, self-paced backoff; heartbeat.py floors at 60 s and fires only into an idle session with an empty queue; state lives in SessionDB state_meta; one dispatch_goal_command serves CLI, gateway, TUI and desktop.
verevonRelevance: A standing-goal loop with deterministic gates is the natural way to make Do mode keep going after approvals, which today does not continue the LLM loop.
notes: Inspired by Codex /goal and Claude Code /loop; zero coverage in earlier Verevon docs for loops and heartbeat.

name: Mixture of Agents as a virtual model provider
what: Named presets appear in every model picker as a provider; reference models advise once per turn and the aggregator is the acting model that owns tool calls and billing.
how: agent/moa_loop.py gathers reference context before each iteration without tool schemas or the system prompt, appends it privately to the aggregator request, merges same-role messages for strict templates; presets are selected through the normal /model machinery (/moa is one-shot sugar); the aggregator is billed for the whole run and the UI marks it as the acting model.
verevonRelevance: A model-comparison or council feature for Verevon can reuse the pattern of exposing an ensemble as one selectable model so tools, interrupts and persistence work unchanged.
notes: Absent from earlier Verevon docs; cost attribution to the aggregator is stated explicitly.

name: Global emergency stop that pauses new work only
what: A sentinel file pauses cron, kanban dispatch and new gateway turns across the install without killing in-flight work, and resumes by deleting the file.
how: agent/estop.py: hermes pause writes $HERMES_HOME/ESTOP (optional JSON reason), checked with one or two uncached os.stat calls on the profile home and the fleet root, fail-safe: a corrupt file or stat error counts as engaged; ported from gastown estop.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has per-run cancel but no tenant-wide 'stop new work' switch; a Control Plane flag read by schedulers and run admission would give operators the same lever.
notes: Covered briefly in earlier docs (estop/pause).

name: Durable cross-process turn lease and stall watchdog
what: Only one process at a time may load, run and flush a given session; the lease is a refreshed database row, and a separate liveness watchdog aborts turns that stall silently.
how: turn_facade_lease.py admits a durable lease (TTL 300 s, wait up to 1,800 s) with a periodic refresher on a shared scheduler, lease loss raises an interrupt attributed to the lease; turn_liveness.py samples an activity clock (600 s default, 15 s poll) and binds the abort to the observed (generation, timestamp) so a turn that resumed is never cancelled; gateway_turn_lease_timeout rejects alias keys waiting more than 5 s.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's session-core is single-writer by design; the stall watchdog bound to an observed generation is a precise recipe for detecting wedged runs without racing resumed ones.
notes: The lease exists because desktop, CLI resume, gateway and background delivery all share one state.db; Verevon's centralised writer avoids that class.

name: Scripted prelude plays tool calls before the first model call
what: A prompt built-in can run a scripted sequence of tool calls, with results fed back to the script, before any model call, producing a normal-looking transcript with no cache mutation.
how: turn_scripted_prelude.py drives a generator yielding (assistant text, tool name, args), runs each through the unchanged run_tool_round with deterministic call ids, counts no API call and fires no api-request hooks, and ends the turn or hands over to the model; used by the initiate_setup onboarding flow.
verevonRelevance: Server-driven guided onboarding or connection checks on the chat page can be played as real tool rows so history, approval and rendering behave exactly as for model-driven calls.

name: Batch runner, trajectory format and trajectory compressor
what: A multiprocessing batch runner executes the agent over a JSONL prompt set with checkpoint resume, tool-usage statistics and from/value trajectories, and a compressor shrinks trajectories to a token budget for training data.
how: batch_runner.py (fire CLI, Pool, per-batch batch_N.jsonl, toolset distributions sampled per prompt, ALL_POSSIBLE_TOOLS schema for stable stats); trajectory_compressor.py protects head and last N turns and summarizes only as much of the middle as needed without splitting tool pairs; agent/trace_upload.py can push traces to Hugging Face.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's trajectory recorder is an in-memory ring buffer with an Atropos export; a resumable batch runner over the public API would make eval and data generation repeatable.
notes: Research tooling rather than product surface; not needed for a web chat app unless Verevon trains models.

name: Live A/B harnesses for tool-visibility and prompt-footprint changes
what: Behaviour changes to the tool surface are validated by running real agents from two pinned checkouts over graded task batteries across several models, with accuracy, turns, tokens and wall time reported.
how: evals/core_tool_deferral and evals/prefix_rediet run each (arm, model, task, rep) in an isolated subprocess with temp HERMES_HOME, hermetic env, seeded DB, deterministic stubs for GUI and browser, programmatic 0-to-1 graders and an orchestrator with resume, parallelism and an infra-abort fuse; 36 eval directories cover compaction, provider fallback, plugin isolation, update pipeline, webhook auth and more.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's eval-lab has 14 offline YAML cases; the A/B-against-a-baseline-checkout method is the missing step before changing tool exposure, deferral thresholds or the learning prompts.
notes: One result is cited in code: deferring clarify dropped structured-clarify usage from 18/18 to 7/18, so it stays eager (tools/tool_search.py:141-145).

name: Independent /review subagent through the async delegation rail
what: /review spawns a full-privilege background reviewer on a fresh context seeded with the last messages, and its result re-enters the originating session as a normal async completion.
how: agent/review_engine.py builds a review goal, passes at most 10 recent messages (12K chars each) as context, routes via auxiliary.review or parent credentials through delegate_task credentials_cfg so credential pools and api_mode detection behave identically, and every surface (CLI, gateway, TUI, desktop) calls start_review.
verevonRelevance: An on-demand independent reviewer over a chat excerpt maps to Verevon's evaluator-optimizer workflow exposed as a button on the chat page.

name: Gateway per-session agent cache with RSS-aware eviction and drain timeouts
what: The messaging gateway keeps warm agents per session (warm prompt prefix plus transcript) with LRU, idle TTL and memory-pressure shedding, and separates drain behaviour for chat turns, cron runs and API runs on restart.
how: gateway.agent_cache max_size 128, idle_ttl 3,600 s, memory_high_mb auto from cgroup limit, max_evictions_per_pass 16, protect_recent 8; restart_after_turn_timeout 1,800 s waits for in-flight work before stop, cron_drain_timeout 30 s floors the drain because an interrupted cron run is a permanent failure; eviction flushes memory under the owning profile's scope.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already drains on /readyz; the per-surface drain floors (cron and API runs never inherit the chat interrupt-immediately default) are a precise detail to copy.

name: Self-registering tool registry with AST-scanned discovery and on-disk verdict cache
what: Dropping a tools/*.py file that calls registry.register() at module top level is enough to add a model tool; no manual import list exists. Startup cost stays low because discovery does not import every module.
how: tools/registry.py discover_builtin_tools() walks tools/*.py plus tools/<pkg>/tool.py, runs a text prefilter then ast.parse to see whether the module body (or a module-level for loop) calls registry.register, and memoizes the verdict on disk keyed by (mtime_ns, size). Only modules that register are imported. A package directory without __init__.py is skipped with a warning because setuptools would drop it from the wheel. ToolRegistry.register() stores schema, handler, toolset, check_fn, requires_env; dispatch() signature-inspects optional kwargs (task_id, session_id, parent_agent) so narrow plugin handlers keep working, wraps every exception into a bounded {error} JSON string and sanitises framing tokens in error text.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's gateway tool_loop.rs has ~30 hand-wired inline tool arms; a declarative registry (schema + handler + availability probe + toolset) with a bounded error-wrapping dispatch is a cheap way to add tools without editing the 3,700-line loop.
notes: Quality 4: the AST prefilter plus disk cache (about 145 ms scan over ~100 files, per the docstring) is a startup-latency trick specific to Python import cost; a Rust port would use inventory/linkme-style static registration instead.

name: Narrow-waist footprint ladder: capability at the edges, not in the core tool list
what: Contributors are pushed to add capability as a CLI command plus skill, a service-gated tool, a plugin or a catalog MCP server before any new core tool, because every tool schema is sent on every API call.
how: Root AGENTS.md states two invariants (prompt-cache stability and narrow waist) and a ladder: extend existing code, CLI command + skill, service-gated tool (check_fn answers reachability, never per-session surface), plugin, MCP catalog server, new core tool last. The rubric rejects hooks with no concrete consumer, new HERMES_* env vars for non-secret config, and core tools that terminal+file or a skill already covers. tools/AGENTS.md repeats it for the registry (about 55 names in _HERMES_CORE_TOOLS).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's chat gateway offers a fixed tool set per turn and Do mode a capability-bound catalogue; adopting an explicit 'prove it cannot be a skill/connector first' rule would keep per-turn schema cost down as connectors multiply.
notes: This is a governance/process finding encoded in the repo's own agent guide, not runtime code. Earlier Verevon docs did not record it.

name: Toolsets and per-platform bundles with surface capability resolved from the session, not the process env
what: Tools are grouped into about 60 named toolsets and about 23 hermes-* platform bundles; GUI-only tools (panes, previews, tours) appear only for sessions that declare a desktop client, even when the backend runs remotely.
how: toolsets.py defines _HERMES_CORE_TOOLS, a TOOLSETS dict via _ts(), and CLIENT_SURFACE_TOOLSETS = {project, desktop_ui, catalog}. The GUI gateway folds these in through _load_enabled_toolsets(platform) based on the session source sent on session.create, never an env var such as HERMES_DESKTOP, because desktop and backend can be on different machines. Untrusted-ingress platforms get a tiny bundle (_HERMES_WEBHOOK_SAFE_TOOLS = web_search, web_extract, vision_analyze, clarify). A 'coding' toolset posture is auto-selected in code workspaces by agent/coding_context.py.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already resolves tool availability per profile (chat vs deployed_agent) in Model Plane; the 'capability is a property of the session client' rule is the right model for browser vs future desktop-app surfaces.
notes: The tool AGENTS guide documents a real bug class: env-keyed gates silently stripped tools on remote topologies.

name: check_fn availability probes cached per profile with schema cross-reference rewriting
what: Each tool declares an availability probe (credentials present, bridge wired) whose result is cached with a TTL per profile, and schema descriptions may not name tools from other toolsets.
how: tools/registry.py keeps _check_fn_cache keyed by hermes_home_key() via check_fn_cache_scope(), with no_cache_check_fn() opt-out and invalidate_check_fn_cache(). Probes must read credentials through agent.secret_scope.get_secret rather than os.getenv, and an UnscopedSecretError at boot is logged at DEBUG. tools/AGENTS.md forbids a schema description naming a tool from another toolset (the model hallucinates calls to unavailable tools); cross-references are added dynamically in model_tools.get_tool_definitions() post-processing blocks.
verevonRelevance: Tool descriptions that reference unavailable tools cause hallucinated calls; Verevon's staged MCP disclosure and per-turn tool pruning could adopt the dynamic cross-reference rule.

name: Profile-scoped registry overlays and plugin override policy
what: One process can serve many profiles; a plugin's tools are registered into that profile's overlay and cannot silently replace a built-in unless the operator allowed it.
how: ToolRegistry holds _tools (global), _scoped_tools keyed by resolved HERMES_HOME, _plugin_override_policy and _plugin_module_scopes; lookups see the profile overlay first; a generation counter is bumped on every mutation and get_tool_definitions memoizes against it; MCP refresh writes are serialised under an RLock with snapshot reads. Delayed callbacks stay confined to the profile that loaded the plugin even after policy removal.
verevonRelevance: Directly relevant to a multi-tenant Model Plane: per-tenant tool overlays with a generation counter and explicit override policy would give org-scoped tools without leaking across tenants.
notes: The multiplexing (many tenants, one process) design is Hermes's answer to what Verevon does with separate service identities and org allowlists.

name: Progressive tool disclosure (tool_search / tool_describe / tool_call bridge)
what: MCP, plugin and some event-triggered core tools are hidden behind three bridge tools so the model sees a compact listing and pulls full schemas on demand.
how: tools/tool_search.py assemble_tool_defs() classifies tools into visible vs deferrable (core and session-gated GUI toolsets never defer unless named in tools.tool_search.defer), replaces deferrable schemas with bridge_tool_schemas(), and embeds a catalog listing in the search tool's description under a token budget min(listing_max_tokens=4000, threshold_pct=5% of context), degrading in tiers full -> names -> bare. The catalog is stateless (rebuilt from live tool-defs every assembly) because a session-keyed catalog drifted and dropped tools. Bridge calls route through model_tools.handle_function_call with local JSON-schema validation of the underlying tool's arguments (tool_search_validation.py) and a cap of 7 queries / 10 describes per call.
verevonRelevance: Verevon collapses MCP to mcp_catalog+mcp_call only above 40 tools and then cannot invoke them; Hermes's tiered, budgeted listing with argument validation and a stateless rebuild is a more general design that also fits provider connectors.
notes: Not in the earlier Verevon Hermes docs (the scout counted zero mentions of tool search). Claude, Codex and Cursor ship comparable deferred-tool schemes; Hermes's version is distinctive for the budgeted listing tiers and eval harness (evals/tool_search).

name: Rarest-token gated BM25 tool search with term-coverage floor
what: Tool search returns relevant tools without flooding results with one-word matches, and tells the model to retry without a token no tool carries.
how: tools/tool_search_catalog.py inlines BM25 (k1=1.5, b=0.75) with Snowball stemming; admission is gated on the query's highest-IDF token (a document without the intent word is not offered, so 'send gmail email' no longer returns incident tools that only share 'email'), plus a MIN_QUERY_TERM_COVERAGE of 0.5 on answerable terms once a query has 4+ terms (introduced after a model re-searched 216 times for 'run shell command execute code python'). Exact name matches rank first and bypass the gate.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon builds connector/MCP discovery, copying the gate-token and coverage rules avoids the observed failure mode of agents looping on low-precision search results.
notes: Comments cite measured failures (216 repeated searches), which is unusually concrete evidence for a retrieval heuristic.

name: In-chat connection operations (manage_connections) as a typed state machine
what: When the agent needs an account or server connected, it raises a card for connectors, MCP servers, plugins or skills; the turn waits until every target is connected, skipped or the deadline passes.
how: tools/connectors/contract.py defines TargetState (pending, initiated, connected, skipped, failed, expired, not_connected), Actor (user, backend_watcher, clock), SettleReason (all_resolved, continue, deadline, interrupt) and a TRANSITIONS table naming the only actor allowed to cause each edge; every 'connected' must be witnessed by the backend (gateway account list, install/OAuth worker), while the card can only skip or retry. operation.py enforces it, live.py keeps one open operation per session, run.py runs the lifecycle; the desktop reads a generated TypeScript copy (connection.request / connection.update / connection.respond RPCs). The tool thread is never parked by the card.
verevonRelevance: A direct pattern for Verevon's OAuth connector onboarding inside chat (Nango/integration-corev2): an actor-guarded transition table prevents the model or UI from asserting 'connected' without backend evidence.
notes: Gateway-backed managed accounts depend on the Nous gateway; the state machine itself is portable.

name: MCP client with supervised transports and a per-call recovery ladder
what: Stdio, Streamable HTTP and SSE MCP servers are connected on one background loop; failures trigger circuit breaking, OAuth refresh, session-expiry reconnect and stdio respawn instead of surfacing raw errors.
how: tools/mcp_tool.py runs each server as a long-lived MCPServerTask on a dedicated asyncio loop thread. mcp_tool_handlers._dispatch chains recoverers (_handle_stdio_child_exited_and_retry, _handle_auth_error_and_retry, _handle_session_expired_and_retry) and only replays tools annotated readOnlyHint=true after session expiry; _check_circuit_breaker implements open/half-open states and distinguishes 'server answered but rejected' from 'unreachable'. mcp_tool_health.py adds list_changed refresh, keepalive probes, lazy verify, in-flight fail-fast and idle/lifetime recycling of stdio children; mcp_tool_lifecycle.py tracks PIDs/PGIDs with start-time fingerprints for orphan cleanup.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's MCP support is registration/OAuth only and the tools cannot be invoked by either loop; Hermes shows the runtime half (recovery, breaker, recycling) that a working invocation path needs.
notes: About 30 mcp_tool_* modules; the most thoroughly engineered MCP client in the reference set.

name: MCP trust tiers with readOnlyHint-based approval of write-capable tools
what: A server marked trust: untrusted can still be used, but any tool lacking a readOnlyHint=true annotation asks the user before running, once per call, fail-closed if the approval system is unavailable.
how: tools/mcp_tool_handlers._trust_gate_check reads the calling profile's trust level (an adopter of a shared connection keeps its own tier), skips read-only tools, and otherwise calls request_elicitation_consent with surface 'mcp-trust/<server>' routed to whichever UI owns the session; deny or cancel returns a tool_error telling the model not to retry without user direction. Trust metadata is captured at registration (mcp_tool_registration) and keyed per profile.
verevonRelevance: Resolves the Verevon blocker where mcp__* tools have no governed capability binding and are denied wholesale: a per-server trust tier plus readOnlyHint classification could bind MCP tools to Ask/Allow capability decisions.
notes: Verevon's earlier docs did not cover this. Risk classification still depends on server-supplied annotations, which an untrusted server can lie about; Hermes treats unannotated as write-capable.

name: MCP supply-chain preflight, managed Node and npx cache swap
what: Before spawning a stdio MCP server Hermes checks the package against OSV malware advisories, runs it on its own managed Node, and avoids leaving a resident npm exec parent.
how: mcp_tool._preflight_stdio_command runs check_package_for_malware off-loop with a 12 s wall-clock bound (fail-open on timeout) before any argv rewriting, then swaps a cached npx package for its direct binary to save ~48 MB per server. mcp_tool_node_abi.py converts NODE_MODULE_VERSION/ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED stderr into a permanent error naming the remedy (rebuild under Hermes's Node). CI adds osv-scanner and supply-chain-audit workflows.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ever admits user-supplied stdio MCP servers (currently quarantined), an OSV malware preflight and managed runtime is the supply-chain control to copy.
notes: Fail-open on timeout is a deliberate trade-off recorded in the code comment.

name: MCP sampling and elicitation handled as bounded host services
what: MCP servers can ask Hermes to run an LLM completion (sampling) or ask the user for structured input (elicitation), under per-server rate limits and caps.
how: tools/mcp_tool_sampling.py implements SamplingHandler and ElicitationHandler. Per-server config: sampling.enabled (default true), model override, max_tokens_cap 4096, timeout 30, max_rpm 10 sliding-window limiter, max_tool_rounds 5, allowed_models, audit log level; elicitation form mode routes through the existing approval surface (CLI/TUI prompt or gateway buttons), URL mode is declined, 300 s timeout.
verevonRelevance: MCP sampling is a prompt-injection and cost vector; the per-server caps and allowed_models list are a ready template if Verevon enables server-initiated inference.
notes: Sampling is on by default in Hermes (when the SDK supports it), which is a more permissive default than a governed enterprise plane would choose.

name: MCP result sanitisation: invisible Unicode tag stripping and reserved _meta filtering
what: Every MCP tool result, resource body and tool description is scrubbed of invisible Unicode TAG characters (U+E0000-E007F) before the model sees it, and protocol-reserved _meta keys are dropped.
how: tools/mcp_tool_handlers imports strip_unicode_tags (tools.ansi_strip) and _strip_reserved_meta_keys; results are capped (_MCP_HARD_RESULT_CAP_CHARS), images are cached to disk and attached natively when the model can see tool-result images, downscaled to vision.embed_target_bytes because they are re-sent every turn.
verevonRelevance: Verevon scans tool results for injection (fail-closed scan + ContentSafety shadow pass) but there is no mention of Unicode tag smuggling; stripping tag characters is a one-line hardening.
notes: Legitimate emoji tag sequences (flags) are preserved.

name: Prompt-cache-preserving MCP refresh and reload confirmation
what: When an MCP server announces new tools, the running agent's tool list is swapped in place while keeping the cached tools[] prefix; /reload-mcp asks before invalidating the provider prompt cache.
how: tools/mcp_tool_agent.py serialises in-place swaps of agent.tools / valid_tool_names under _agent_tools_lock, preserves the cached prefix across rebuilds and re-injects post-build tools; approvals.mcp_reload_confirm (default true) warns that tool schemas live in the system prompt so the next message re-sends full input tokens.
verevonRelevance: Dynamic tool changes are a hidden cache-cost trap; Verevon's Anthropic cache_control breakpoints on tools would be broken by the same event, so a confirm-or-defer rule is worth copying.

name: Profile-scoped MCP connection ledger with adoption of matching shared connections
what: Two profiles configuring the same named MCP server with different credentials get two connections; a profile may adopt another's live connection only when route and credentials match.
how: tools/mcp_tool_scope.py keys every ledger (_servers, errors, cooldowns, circuit breaker, lazy configs, trust metadata) by ServerKey = name or (owner_scope, name) under a multiplexer; _server_tool_scopes[key] records adopters and _resolve_server_key finds a shared connection. Prior name-only keying left a second profile permanently tool-less.
verevonRelevance: A tenant-keyed connection ledger is exactly what Verevon needs if MCP servers are shared per org vs per user (/v1/mcp/servers share).

name: Curated MCP catalog (optional-mcps) with manifests, trust note and composer suggestions
what: Users install vendor MCP servers (65 manifests such as context7, notion, linear, stripe) with one click, choose tools at install time, and are shown the exact source, bootstrap commands and endpoint before installing.
how: optional-mcps/<name>/manifest.yaml (manifest_version, transport http/stdio, auth, post_install, suggest.keywords/hosts for composer brand pills, optional install.bootstrap). Presence in the directory equals approval via PR review. The dashboard MCP page and the picker print the source URL; ${ENV_VAR} substitution happens at runtime; per-server include/exclude name filters with glob precedence rules and utility-tool filtering.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has MCP register/share endpoints but no curated catalogue; a manifest-with-trust-note format reviewed through PRs is a low-cost way to ship vetted connectors.

name: Hermes as an MCP server (messaging bridge and Codex tool callback)
what: hermes mcp serve exposes conversations as MCP tools to any MCP client, and a second stdio MCP server hands a curated Hermes toolset to the Codex runtime.
how: mcp_serve.py builds an mcp.server.MCPServer over stdio with 9 channel-bridge tools plus channels_list (list conversations, read history, send, poll events, manage approvals). agent/transports/hermes_tools_mcp_server.py is spawned by codex app-server and dispatches calls through model_tools.handle_function_call, the same path as the default runtime.
verevonRelevance: Exposing Model Plane threads/runs as an MCP server would let Claude Code, Cursor or Codex drive Verevon agents; Verevon has HTTP/gRPC but no outward MCP server.

name: Plugin system with kinds, one ctx surface and a 'plugins never touch core' rule
what: General plugins add tools, hooks, CLI subcommands, slash commands, locales and context references; specialised kinds add memory providers, model providers, context engines, image/video/web backends, browser backends, terminal environments, cron providers, dashboard auth and platform adapters.
how: hermes_cli/plugins.py PluginManager discovers bundled, $HERMES_HOME/plugins, ./.hermes/plugins (opt-in via HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS) and pip entry points, later-wins; memory providers are bundled-first and single-select. Each kind has an ABC + orchestrator (agent/memory_provider.py, context_engine.py, image_gen_provider.py) and its own discovery. Policy: a plugin must not modify run_agent.py, cli.py or gateway/run.py; missing capability means widening the generic ctx/hook surface. New in-tree memory providers and third-party-product plugins are closed; they ship as catalog entries.
verevonRelevance: The Model Plane plugin CRUD is stub-level ('inert until a host loads its manifest'); Hermes shows a working kind-by-kind plugin architecture whose hook vocabulary and ctx API could define what a Verevon plugin host loads.
notes: Codex and Claude Code have plugin systems; Hermes's distinguishing feature is the number of backend kinds and the isolation host.

name: 44-name hook vocabulary split into observers, transforms and vetoes with fail-closed policy hooks
what: Plugins and shell scripts can observe or alter tool calls, LLM calls, streams, approvals, sessions, gateway dispatch, transcription and kanban events; a hung policy hook blocks the tool instead of letting it through.
how: hermes_cli/plugins.py VALID_HOOKS holds 44 names (pre/post_tool_call, transform_tool_result, transform_terminal_output, transform_llm_output, pre/post_llm_call, pre/post_api_request, api_request_error, pre/post_auxiliary_call, transform_api_error_classification, on_session_*, on_stream_*, pre_verify, pre_gateway_dispatch, post_gateway_admission, pre/post_approval, on_human_input_*, pre_transcription, subagent_start/stop, pre_command, kanban events, gateway_platform_event, on_room_member_activity). invoke_hook returns non-None results; hot-path hooks and pre_tool_call are bounded by plugins.hook_callback_timeout (30 s) with abandoned workers, pre_tool_call timeouts fail closed with a block directive, other bounded hooks fail open. Callbacks are signature-inspected so narrow signatures get only declared kwargs. New hook names land only with real fire-sites.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's hook engine is real but its registry is in-memory and Do mode passes an empty hook_context; a versioned hook vocabulary with explicit fail-open/fail-closed semantics per hook is the contract to adopt.
notes: The scout's inventory counted 33 hook names; counting quoted names in VALID_HOOKS gives 44 at HEAD b236008.

name: Middleware contract (request rewrite and execution wrap) separate from observers
what: Observers report what happened; middleware can rewrite a tool/LLM request or wrap the actual execution callback, with schema-versioned payloads.
how: hermes_cli/middleware.py defines VALID_MIDDLEWARE = {tool_request, tool_execution, llm_request, llm_execution}, OBSERVER_SCHEMA_VERSION 'hermes.observer.v1' and MIDDLEWARE_SCHEMA_VERSION 'hermes.middleware.v1', RequestMiddlewareResult with a change trace, and a safe deep-copy that tolerates non-copyable request members. invoke_middleware/has_middleware in plugins.py lazy-discover plugins so every surface sees the same delivery.
verevonRelevance: A rewrite/wrap middleware layer is how Verevon could add redaction, PII or ZDR transformations around inference-core calls as pluggable policy rather than gateway code.

name: Shell-script hooks with Claude-Code-compatible block semantics and first-use consent
what: Users can wire hooks: entries in config.yaml to arbitrary scripts; exit code 2 blocks a pre_tool_call (like Claude Code and Cursor) and each (event, command) pair needs one-time consent.
how: agent/shell_hooks.py registers config hooks as callbacks on the plugin hook manager; payload is stdin JSON {hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input, session_id, cwd, extra}; stdout JSON may return decision/action block|modify or context; default timeout 60 s (max 300); fails open unless fail_closed; consent recorded in shell-hooks-allowlist.json under HERMES_HOME with a file lock; registrations keyed by (home, event, matcher, command) so multiplexed profiles stay separate.
verevonRelevance: Verevon cannot apply hooks in Do mode today; a shell/HTTP hook adapter honouring the Claude Code exit-code convention would give enterprises a familiar policy extension point.
notes: Claude Code's hooks are the reference; Hermes matches them intentionally.

name: Plugin host isolation: third-party plugins in a per-profile child process over a framed protocol
what: With plugins.isolation: host, every non-bundled plugin runs in a separate process that exposes tools, hooks, commands and provider objects through proxies; an operator-pinned setting in /etc/hermes beats the user's own config.
how: hermes_cli/plugin_host.py (parent), plugin_host_child.py, plugin_host_wire.py (framed JSON); the child receives a RemotePluginContext. Invariants: every user-code import path routes to the host or refuses (general plugins, memory/context/cron providers, model-provider profiles through credential-free extraction cached by file fingerprint, dashboard APIs through an ASGI bridge); HOST_UNSUPPORTED_CTX_METHODS is one table read by the runtime refusal and the static audit (plugin_isolation_audit.py); a host never spawns a host; isolation_mode() reads through the managed overlay. Per-profile env comes from served_profile_child_env.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's plugin host does not exist yet; an out-of-process plugin boundary with a static audit of what cannot cross is the safer starting point than in-process loading.
notes: SECURITY.md still states plugins are in-process and trusted by default; the host mode is opt-in hardening, not the default.

name: Behaviour-based plugin compatibility contract instead of a global API version
what: Plugin authors rely on additive hook payloads, never-removed ctx methods and signature-inspected callbacks; deprecations follow a once-per-process warning and at least two minor releases.
how: plugins/AGENTS.md summarises the contract: hook payload data added as keyword fields, PluginContext methods never removed or renamed, unknown manifest fields ignored, new provider methods get defaults, a local schema version only where a wire/persisted contract exists. Compat tests load frozen plugins through real discovery. Internal import paths are explicitly not API: after the 2026-09-14 window an old path raises ImportError shown as the plugin's load error.
verevonRelevance: Gives Verevon a pre-agreed compatibility stance before any plugin host ships, avoiding a PLUGIN_API_VERSION treadmill.

name: Plugin catalog: SHA-pinned entries, kill list and installer-owned provenance
what: Out-of-tree plugins are discovered only through a catalog of about 570 YAML entries, each pinned to a 40-hex commit; removed.yaml blocks known-bad repos on every install path and again at update, enable and load.
how: plugin-catalog/<name>.yaml (repo, sha, subdir, version, tier, category, capabilities.provides_tools/hooks/middleware, requires_env, a disclosure sentence on data sent); plugin-catalog-ci.yml clones each changed entry at its pin and runs hermes plugins validate; hermes_cli/plugin_catalog.py + plugins_cmd_catalog.py resolve names (no second name index), refresh live from the docs build with an in-tree fallback; provenance lives on the installer-owned .install-metadata.json, never in the plugin tree (a repo can ship a forged .hermes-catalog.json); repo URLs compare by canonical host/owner/repo; --allow-removed is CLI-only and recorded.
verevonRelevance: A pin-plus-kill-list marketplace with data-disclosure text per entry is a concrete governance model for a Verevon extension marketplace.
notes: Entries include a 'disclosure' sentence (e.g. what is sent to a memory vendor), which matches ZDR/privacy needs.

name: Skills: SKILL.md packs with enforced authoring standards and one slash command per skill
what: Skills are directories with SKILL.md frontmatter, scripts, references and templates; 58 are bundled, 155 optional, and each becomes a /<name> command that injects as a user message.
how: Frontmatter: name, description (<= 60 chars, one sentence, enforced by tests/skills/test_authoring_standards.py), version, author, platforms OS gate, metadata.hermes.tags/category/related_skills/config (stored under skills.config.<key>, prompted at setup). Standard section order (When to Use, Prerequisites, How to Run, Quick Reference, Procedure, Pitfalls, Verification), helper scripts instead of inline parsers, no offset/limit pagination on skill-loading tools. agent/skill_commands.py scans ~/.hermes/skills and injects the skill as a user message, never into the system prompt, to preserve the cache.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already matches up to 3 skills per turn and injects with a budget; the 60-char description rule and the 'no pagination on instructional tools' rule are cheap quality gates to adopt.
notes: Skills follow the agentskills.io format shared with Claude and Codex.

name: Skills Guard and Plugin Guard: trust-tiered scanner with an un-overridable dangerous verdict
what: Skills and plugins from outside the repo are statically scanned; community content with any finding is blocked, trusted repos may carry cautions, agent-created skills ask only on dangerous findings, and plugin installs can never be forced past a 'dangerous' verdict.
how: tools/skills_guard.py SCANNER_VERSION skills-guard-v10, INSTALL_POLICY matrix {builtin, trusted, community, agent-created} x {safe, caution, dangerous}, TRUSTED_REPOS (openai/skills, anthropics/skills, huggingface/skills, NVIDIA/skills; NVIDIA skills ship a signed skill.oms.sig). tools/plugin_guard.py reuses the engine with plugin-sized limits and context exemptions (own-secret reads allowed on code, full patterns on docs/config where injection lives); skills_ast_audit.py adds AST checks. SECURITY.md says the guard is a review aid, not a boundary.
verevonRelevance: A trust-tier x verdict policy matrix for skill ingestion is directly reusable for Verevon's learned and shared skills (session-core agent_skills).

name: Skills Hub with multiple sources and GitHub-App-authenticated search
what: Users install skills from GitHub repos, LobeHub, a well-known-endpoint source, ClawHub, skills.sh and the in-repo optional-skills tree.
how: tools/skills_hub.py plus skills_hub_sources.py, skills_hub_official.py (OptionalSkillSource), skills_hub_clawhub.py, skills_hub_skillssh.py, skills_hub_install.py, skills_hub_search.py; GitHub App JWT auth via PyJWT; skills index cache built by scripts/build_skills_index.py; hermes skills install official/<category>/<skill>.
verevonRelevance: Low priority: Verevon's skills are org-scoped rather than public-hub installs; useful only for an eventual marketplace.
notes: Not in the earlier Verevon docs (skills hub / ClawHub had zero mentions).

name: Single slash-command registry feeding CLI, gateway, Telegram/Slack menus, autocomplete and the desktop palette
what: A command defined once appears everywhere with consistent aliases, categories, mid-run behaviour and desktop disposition.
how: hermes_cli/commands.py CommandDef(name, description, category, aliases, args_hint, subcommands, cli_only, gateway_only, gateway_config_gate, busy_policy dispatch|reject|interrupt_then_dispatch, busy_handler, execute, argument_mode, desktop, desktop_subcommands) in COMMAND_REGISTRY (103 entries). Dispatch is table-driven (_SLASH_DISPATCH, _command_handler_table) with no elif ladders; the live commands.catalog RPC carries the desktop disposition and a generated JSON registry is the offline fallback with drift tests.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's command catalogue (/models, /compact) exists in capability-core but the composer does not use it; a single registry with busy_policy and surface flags is the model to finish.

name: @-reference expansion with plugin-extensible prefixes
what: Users type @file:, @folder:, @diff, @git:, @url: (and plugin prefixes such as @issue:) in a prompt and the references are expanded into context with autocomplete.
how: agent/context_references.py BUILTIN_PREFIXES = {diff, staged, file, folder, git, url}; ContextReferenceProvider ABC (prefix, description, async autocomplete(), expand()) registered via PluginContext.register_context_reference(); safety imports HOME_CREDENTIAL_DIRS to avoid reading credential directories; hardened non-interactive git argv.
verevonRelevance: A provider-extensible @-mention mechanism could back Verevon 'attach knowledge/connector item' pills without core changes.

name: ctx.llm: host-owned, trust-gated LLM access for plugins
what: A plugin can make one-shot chat or structured-JSON LLM calls (sync or async) using the user's active provider without ever seeing a credential; an unconfigured plugin cannot choose its own model or credentials.
how: ctx.llm.complete / complete_structured / acomplete / acomplete_structured; results carry text, parsed (validated against a JSON schema if jsonschema is installed), usage, provider, model and an audit field with the plugin-supplied purpose string; credentials, pools and aux overrides stay host-side; operators opt in per plugin in config.yaml to override provider/model/agent.
verevonRelevance: The right shape for letting Verevon plugins/skills call models through Model Plane with attribution, budgets and ZDR resolved centrally.
notes: Docs-only evidence here; implementation lives under hermes_cli/plugins*.py and was not read end to end.

name: OpenAI-compatible API server with runs, idempotency, capability discovery and profile-prefixed mirrors
what: Any OpenAI-compatible frontend can use Hermes at /v1; richer clients get /v1/runs with events, approvals, steer and stop, /api/sessions, /api/jobs for cron, artifacts upload/download and a machine-readable /v1/capabilities.
how: gateway/platforms/api_server.py (aiohttp) route table _http_route_table(): /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses (get/delete by id), /v1/models, /v1/capabilities, /v1/skills, /v1/toolsets, /api/sessions CRUD + fork + chat + chat/stream + model lock, /api/jobs pause/resume/run, /api/platforms/{p}/events, /api/cron/fire (JWT from the managed cron service). api_server_runs.py adds POST /v1/runs, GET /v1/runs/{id}, /events, /approval, /steer, /stop; run_idempotency in SQLite with owner pid/start-time. Every route is mirrored under /p/{profile}/ by a prefix middleware. The adapter refuses to start without a strong API_SERVER_KEY (>=16 chars) even on loopback and marks a bad key non-retryable to avoid reconnect-loop fd leaks.
verevonRelevance: Verevon exposes /v1/invoke and /v1/runs but no OpenAI-compatible surface; adding /v1/chat/completions and /v1/responses facades would let Open WebUI, Cursor-style clients and scripts use Verevon agents.
notes: Auth is a single shared bearer key per profile, so it is single-tenant by design (SECURITY.md rule 4: callers within the allowlist are equally trusted).

name: A2A protocol client and server (Agent Card, both directions)
what: Hermes can discover and call other A2A-compliant agents and can itself be called as an A2A agent via an Agent Card at /.well-known/agent-card.json.
how: plugins/platforms/a2a (plugin.yaml kind: platform; adapter.py, protocol.py, security.py, tools.py, DESIGN.md): outbound tools a2a_discover, a2a_call, a2a_list, a2a_history, a2a_orchestrate; inbound tasks are routed into the agent's live gateway session; security defaults: no bearer token configured means localhost-only bind, inbound text passes prompt-injection filters, outbound text is scrubbed of credential-shaped strings, every exchange audit-logged and persisted outside the compaction pipeline; pure stdlib transport.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's baseline lists no ACP, AG-UI or A2A; an A2A adapter would let Verevon agents interoperate with Google ADK/LangChain/CrewAI peers behind the existing capability policy.
notes: Implementation files not read beyond the manifest; maturity of the A2A code is unverified.

name: Desktop and dashboard plugin SDKs with slot registries and hot reload
what: The native desktop app is contribution-driven: panes, routes, sidebar nav, status-bar items, palette commands, keybinds and themes register into one registry, and a single-file ESM plugin dropped into the plugins directory hot-reloads; the web dashboard has a separate slot-based plugin system.
how: @hermes/plugin-sdk exposes host.state.* (readonly nanostore views), curated host actions, host.request (gateway JSON-RPC), ctx.rest/ctx.socket for a plugin_api.py backend namespace /api/plugins/<id>. Four in-tree desktop examples (hello-runtime, hermes-bots, kanban, radio). The dashboard uses window.__HERMES_PLUGINS__.registerSlot with named slots (header-left, sidebar, pre-main, page-scoped sessions:top, ...) declared in manifest.json. Docs warn that 'plugin' means three unrelated systems here.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon's SolidJS frontend wants third-party panels, a single-import SDK plus slot registry (core registers through the same API) avoids a bolted-on extension story.
notes: Not an API Verevon needs soon; relevant to the 'agent pages' surface extensibility.

name: Programmatic integration through three protocols over one AIAgent core
what: External programs choose ACP (editors), the TUI-gateway JSON-RPC (custom hosts) or the OpenAI-compatible HTTP+SSE API, all driving the same agent.
how: Documented in programmatic-integration.md with a method catalogue (prompt.submit, session.steer, session.branch, session.compress, session.interrupt, reload.mcp, subagent.steer, spawn_tree.*) and a Pi-style RPC mapping table (prompt, steer, follow_up, abort, set_model, compact, get_state, get_messages).
verevonRelevance: Verevon has HTTP+SSE and gRPC but no editor-protocol or documented RPC mapping; publishing a protocol-mapping table would be a cheap SDK win.

name: Pluggable terminal backends behind one spawn-per-call shell contract
what: The same terminal, execute_code and file tools run on the local host, Docker, Singularity/Apptainer, SSH, Modal (direct or Nous-managed), Daytona or Vercel Sandbox by changing terminal.backend.
how: tools/environments/base.py BaseEnvironment spawns a fresh bash -c per command; a session snapshot (env vars, functions, aliases) is captured once and re-sourced before each command, and CWD persists through in-band stdout markers (remote) or a temp file (local). base_output.py defines a ProcessHandle Protocol and _ThreadedProcessHandle so SDK-only backends (Modal, Daytona, Vercel) satisfy the same handle through a background thread; foreground commands run in their own process group and a process-exit funnel kills them. The file tools are implemented on top of the shell contract, so a backend's mounts bound them too.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's sandbox-manager is lease bookkeeping with execution in execution-core's own container; a ProcessHandle-style seam would let Verevon add remote sandboxes without rewriting timeout/cancel logic.
notes: Earlier Verevon docs already adopted the ProcessHandle idea (decisions ledger 'defer a SandboxBackend trait'); the spawn-per-call plus env-snapshot model and in-band CWD markers are the part not recorded there.
