what: An external connector service fronts platforms such as Discord or Telegram; the gateway dials out, receives a CapabilityDescriptor (limits, draft streaming, edit, threads, markdown dialect, ops supported) and exchanges normalised events and actions, without knowing the concrete platform.
how: gateway/relay (adapter, auth, command_manifest, descriptor, egress, media, transport, ws_transport) implements contract v1 (experimental, additive-only gated by contract_version); descriptor fields max_message_length, supports_draft_streaming/edit/threads/context/inchannel_continuable/block_formatting, markdown_dialect, len_unit (chars vs utf16), supported_ops for op-level discovery; inbound frames travel on the same socket the gateway dialled; token-less follow_up ops; scale_to_zero.py self-suspends the machine after go_dormant() while wake stays platform-side.
verevonRelevance: A capability-descriptor handshake is a sound way for Verevon's Channel Plane to front Slack/Teams/WhatsApp without each adapter leaking platform quirks into Model Plane.
notes: Experimental per its own docstring.

name: ACP server for editors with permission, edit-approval and provenance bridges
what: hermes acp speaks the Agent Client Protocol over stdio so VS Code, Zed and JetBrains can create, load, resume, fork and list sessions, stream message and tool-call updates, request permissions and show diffs.
how: acp_adapter (server.py ~1,100 lines, session.py, events.py, tools.py, permissions.py, edit_approval.py, model_catalog.py, commands.py, provenance.py, auth.py): ThreadPoolExecutor(4) runs the synchronous AIAgent off the event loop; permission options allow_once/allow_session/allow_always/deny/deny_always map to Hermes approval results (ACP has no session-scoped kind so Hermes semantics ride the option id); EditProposal approval is bound in a ContextVar only for ACP runs so CLI and gateway bypass it; session provenance under _meta.hermes derives previous/current internal ids and lineage root from the compression chain so the editor-facing session_id stays stable across compaction; MCP servers passed in new_session are registered per session; interrupted prompts are rewritten and queued; cancel also stops background delegation units for the session.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's baseline lists no ACP; exposing a read-only ACP or A2A facade would let editors and agent frameworks use Verevon runs, with approvals mapped to Verevon HITL options.
notes: Not in earlier Verevon docs. ACP has no goal command or goal loop yet (hermes_cli/AGENTS.md).

name: SQLite state.db with WAL read pool, FTS5 (CJK tokenizer), lineage and self-repair
what: All sessions, messages, usage, gateway routing, turn leases, compression locks and async delegations live in one SQLite database per profile, with search across history and tooling to repair, back up, export and import it.
how: hermes_state.py facade plus 34 hermes_state_*.py siblings; schema version 31 with tables sessions, messages, system_prompts, session_model_usage, state_meta, gateway_routing, gateway_hygiene_state, conversation_generations, gateway_heartbeats, compression_locks, session_turn_leases, async_delegations; FTS5 indexes messages_fts and trigram, with a loadable CJK-bigram tokenizer built from native/fts5_cjk (trigram needs 3+ chars so 1-2 char CJK terms fell back to LIKE scans); sessions carry parent_session_id and end_reason for compression lineage; read-connection pool with per-file and process ceilings and fd-headroom gate; hermes_state_lockowners reads /proc/locks to name who holds the WAL write lock; repair/lost-and-found via SQLite .recover; a test-isolation guard raises before a pytest-context process opens a live state.db; Dockerfile builds a pinned SQLite to avoid the WAL-reset bug.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has Postgres but no server-side conversation search; a CJK-aware FTS index and per-session lineage would be the model for thread search (Norwegian needs a stemming tokenizer, not CJK).
notes: Single-writer SQLite is right for a personal agent; Verevon's multi-tenant Postgres would use tsvector/pg_trgm instead.

name: Config system: three loaders, atomic comment-preserving writes, defaults with readers, secrets-only .env
what: config.yaml holds settings and .env holds secrets only; every key in DEFAULT_CONFIG must have a reader and every reader a registered key; writes round-trip comments and refuse to delete by omission.
how: hermes_cli/config.py: DEFAULT_CONFIG deep-merges new keys (bump _config_version only to migrate), OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS registry for secrets; load_cli_config (CLI), load_config (setup/tools), load_user_config_effective (gateway, TUI, cron, doctor: user file + managed overlay + ${VAR} expansion + model-key canon, no defaults) with an explicit 'wrong loader' diagnosis rule; one writer seam atomic_config_write / atomic_config_replace through ruamel round-trip with a fail-closed unreadable-file guard and a CI lint (check_config_yaml_writers.py) banning yaml.dump on config paths; cli-config.yaml.example is a 127 KB reference.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's configuration spans env vars across many services; the 'every key has a reader' invariant test would catch dead knobs in Model Plane's 100+ env settings.

name: Transactional self-update pipeline with fleet-wide drain and a frozen compatibility surface
what: hermes update plans, snapshots every profile, applies, restarts each service kind drain-first, verifies and reports; interrupted restarts leave obligations; old updaters that import new code keep working through frozen entry points.
how: hermes_cli/update_cmd*.py with update_fleet_scope (restarts bounded by the home each unit runs on), update_handoff.py and update_serve_obligations.py frozen by tests/compat/old_updater_surface.json, snapshots with one identical file set for every profile, Windows ZIP fallback only when git itself failed and the tree is clean, receipts in logs/update_receipts, post-commit failures exit 0 as owed follow-ups; completion runs in a fresh bootstrap Python that asks PM to sync extras before any application import; desktop adds bundle-swap and bundle-skew detection so a new runtime never runs under an old renderer; Windows App Installer owns packaged updates.
verevonRelevance: Relevant to Verevon's signed-artifact v3 runner and the 'desktop and runtime update on separate clocks' problem if a local connector or desktop app is added.

name: Release channels, native installers and distribution matrix
what: Hermes ships through preview, stable, canary and source-branch channels with an installer matrix: install.sh/ps1, a Tauri bootstrap installer, MSIX/App Installer on Windows, Termux APT repo, Docker images and a Nix flake with NixOS and home-manager modules.
how: hermes_cli/release_channels.py validates an R2 channel wire protocol (policies preview, stable-release, canary-release, source-branch; names are data; 64-hex SHA-256, 40-hex commit, 32-hex build id; bounded metadata 4 MiB; never a silent fallback); apps/bootstrap-installer is a Tauri 2 crate (the only Rust in the tree) whose bootstrap.rs is a direct port of the Electron runBootstrap: resolves install script, lists stages from -Manifest, runs each stage with up to 3 attempts, streams events over a Tauri channel and writes a forensic log; Electron uses electron-updater, MSIX bundles and macOS bundle swaps; docker.yml, nix/ modules, scripts/termux APT repo; 54 GitHub workflows including install E2E on Linux/macOS/Windows.
verevonRelevance: The Tauri installer is a worked example of a stage-runner with retries and forensic logs that could be reimplemented in Rust for a Verevon desktop/connector installer.
notes: Not in earlier Verevon docs (Tauri/bootstrap installer had zero mentions).

name: Code-health ratchet and agent-readable fix text enforced in CI
what: New functions must stay under cyclomatic complexity 20, 300 lines and nesting 6, files under 2,000 lines; already-over units can only shrink; each rule's 'fix' text is written for the coding agent that trips it.
how: scripts/code_health/config.py TARGETS {CC 20, FUNC_LINES 300, NESTING 6, FILE_LINES 2000} measured per unit against the base revision, ENFORCEMENT read from main (blocking|advisory|off) so a PR cannot relax its own check, Rule(id, title, fix, source ruff|ast|regex, exclude, include) for HX profile-scope rules and others; scripts/check runs every blocking lint with CI's pinned tools and can install a pre-push hook; facade + sibling layout rules (behaviour in siblings, never facades; late-import the facade; patch where production reads); root AGENTS.md capped at 12k chars and each root-to-area chain at 30k so guides load whole on 128k models.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's 3,700-line invoke_stream_sse and 13.5k-line agent.rs are exactly what a per-unit ratchet prevents; the agent-facing fix text and size-capped AGENTS guides are low-cost adoptions for AI-assisted Rust development.
notes: Process insight rather than product feature.

name: Desktop typed capability bridge: renderer without Node access and about 170 ipcMain handlers
what: The renderer cannot reach Node or Electron directly; native power (filesystem, git, windows, terminals, updates, clipboard, notifications) arrives through narrow typed IPC capabilities.
how: apps/desktop/electron registers about 167 ipcMain.handle channels named hermes:* (git, hud, fs, connections, window, pet-overlay, terminal, quick-entry, profile, cloud, bootstrap, logs, context-menu ...), the preload exposes typed capabilities, state is placed by authority (backend for anything another surface can change, Electron for machine facts, renderer for presentation), persisted renderer state declares its scope in its key (global, connection, profile, session, project, window), and context switches are soft re-homes (connection) versus hard re-homes (HERMES_HOME).
verevonRelevance: If Verevon adds a desktop wrapper, the 'decide state by authority' rule and scope-in-the-key convention prevent cross-org state bleed in the client.
notes: IPC count measured with grep over non-test files; the scout's figure of about 200 counted prefixes including events.

name: Desktop connection ladder across local, remote, SSH and Cloud backends
what: One desktop app registers named gateways (local runtime, remote HTTP, SSH host, Hermes Cloud) and runs agents on all of them side by side with persistent connections and background streaming.
how: Settings -> Gateways registry with Local, Remote gateway (session token or OAuth), SSH (app opens the tunnel, starts the dashboard and adopts a token) and Cloud (portal discovery); every seam resolves through one ordered ladder where precedence is data, a candidate is trusted only after it is probed, a failed read falls to the next rung but a failed authoritative write surfaces or rolls back, retries are bounded and end in a recovery affordance; OAuth gateway connections mint a fresh ticket per dial and only a confirmed 401/403 means reauth; every REST call against a pooled backend carries ?profile=.
verevonRelevance: Matches the hybrid local/cloud runtime question for Verevon connectors; the ladder rules are a reusable resolver policy.

name: Session identity layers: durable at send, runtime id, lineage root
what: A session has a durable id, a runtime id and a lineage-root id that survives compression rotation; the user's message is written durably before the turn runs, and a verifiably gone session drops to a fresh draft that adopts the unsent text.
how: apps/desktop AGENTS.md 'Identity is not incidental': prompt.submit writes session and user rows first and the turn adopts that row (#111868); compression rotates the internal head while ACP/editor ids and prompt-cache scope resolve to the lineage root (acp_adapter/provenance, agent/prompt_cache_scope); subagent snapshots follow the conversation through durable lineage (owner_agent_session_id -> compression tip) because desktop reconnect remints the UI session id.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane's thread/run ids are stable but compaction summaries are persisted as messages; making lineage root an explicit field would simplify caching, resume and subagent attribution.

name: Rust-portability assessment of Hermes's runtime design
what: Which parts of Hermes translate to Rust cleanly and which depend on Python threading and dynamic loading.
how: Portable: tool registry contract (JSON-string handlers, check_fn, schema collection), phase-pipeline turn loop (phases return break/continue/return), JSON-RPC with generated contracts, 44-name hook vocabulary with signature-inspected kwargs (becomes versioned payload structs), additive SQLite migrations, provider profiles as data, approval floors as pure functions over normalised command strings. Python-specific: contextvar-bound profile scope (becomes task-local tenant context), AST-based tool discovery (becomes inventory/linkme), thread-blocking server requests (becomes oneshot channels), in-process plugin loading (becomes a process or WASM host, which Hermes's plugin_host already approximates), ruamel round-trip YAML writes. The only Rust in the tree is the Tauri installer.
verevonRelevance: Guides the Rust re-creation: copy contracts, phase tables, registries and floors; replace contextvars, threads and dynamic imports with typed tenant context, tasks and an out-of-process plugin host.
notes: Inference from reading the architecture; no Rust prototype was attempted.

name: Guides as architecture: size-capped AGENTS.md hierarchy plus long-form developer docs
what: Each area has an AGENTS.md that loads automatically when working there, with a routing table at the root and long-form docs under website/docs/developer-guide; the structure is itself tested for size.
how: Root AGENTS.md (hub, 12k cap), per-area AGENTS.md (agent, hermes_cli, gateway, tools, plugins, tui_gateway, web, apps/desktop, skills, cron, pm, tests, hermes_platform), scripts/check enforces the 12k root cap and 30k per root-to-area chain; AGENTS.md rules cite issue numbers and incidents; website docs hold about 58 developer-guide pages.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's CLAUDE.md plus stale docs register shows the opposite problem (docs drift); a size-capped, tested guide hierarchy keeps agent guidance current.

name: Bot Mode: profiles as persistent named agents with group chats and bot-to-bot messaging
what: Each profile becomes a Bot with its own role, model, memory, skills, avatar, a permanent 'Bot Chat', routines, group rooms of 2-6 bots and direct bot-to-bot messages, shown in a roster inside the desktop app.
how: Bot = Hermes profile (no new primitive); canonical Bot Chat identified by (profile, session titled exactly 'Bot Chat') via a UNIQUE(title) index, resolved by session.list {title, include_hidden}, with no stored session-id pointer (five prior pointer-based fixes regressed); /new in a Bot Chat is rerouted to /compact; group rooms live in gateway/hosted_rooms*.py (append-only event log, protocol v2, caps such as 128 members/50,000 events per room, 90-day disbanded tombstones), hosted_room_driver/discussion/peer/policy_checkpoint, a target-issued execution policy per member turn, serial rounds (max 3 rounds, 10 messages per send) that settle when a full round is silent, @mention routing, stop directives only adjacent to an @mention, per-member hidden room session with Compress history; rooms mirror into every connected gateway with per-gateway versioning; hermes peer sends bot-initiated DMs across machines through a relay; 'warm backends' bound how many bots run at once.
verevonRelevance: A shipped multi-agent group-chat and 'persistent teammate' UX that neither Claude desktop nor Manus has; relevant to Verevon agent pages (fleet console, chatbot studio) and to Model Plane's currently stub-level coordinator/team mode.
notes: Identity-by-name (not by pointer) is a transferable lesson: the maintainers record that pointer-based identity dangled repeatedly.

name: Session branching and whole-session fork as first-class RPCs and API routes
what: A conversation can be branched (visible history copied into a new session in the parent's profile) from the TUI/desktop, forked via ACP fork_session or POST /api/sessions/{id}/fork.
how: tui_gateway/methods_session_branch.py (session.branch, session.branch_whole) copies user/assistant rows with visible text as full copies (reasoning and timeline-marker tags survive), builds the branched agent in the parent's profile with a dedicated db handle transferred to the agent, and registers it; the API server exposes /api/sessions/{id}/fork; ACP implements fork_session; prompt-cache scope treats fork children as isolated scopes while compression rotation keeps the lineage root.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no server-side branch model (sessions.proto has no parent/sibling fields) and edit versions are client-only; Hermes's fork-by-copy with lineage metadata is a straightforward design.

name: Separated observability planes with unconditional fail-closed redaction
what: Operational health goes to an operator-configured OTLP endpoint with no content; opt-in aggregate product metrics go to the vendor; trajectories and content-bearing telemetry are a separate integration; every exported string is redacted.
how: agent/monitoring: in-process emitter (fire-and-forget queue that never blocks or raises into gateway code, nothing persisted), typed events (GatewayHealthEvent, GatewayDiagnosticEvent), otlp_exporter.py (optional OpenTelemetry extra, no default destination, headers_env read at export time), gateway_health_export, cron_health, a resettable pseudonymous install id (service.instance.id), redaction.py redact_for_export (secrets via redact_for_egress that fails closed if the redactor is broken, then PII shapes email/phone/UUID); explicitly out of scope: prompts, messages, tool args, session history, audit records, product analytics.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane has Prometheus and OTEL but a mixed content/no-content story under ZDR; separating a content-free ops plane from content-bearing traces with a fail-closed redactor is a clean rule.

name: Context-window breakdown with provenance and honest estimates
what: /context shows how the window is spent across system prompt tiers, tool schemas, rules files, skills, MCP, memory and conversation, labelling occupancy as provider-reported or estimated.
how: agent/context_breakdown.py estimates system prompt tiers, tool schemas and history for the category breakdown; overall occupancy keeps its provider-usage or estimate provenance and category figures are explicitly not tokenizer counts or gate authority; zero-token categories are kept for the conversation so an empty transcript is not indistinguishable from an unmeasured one; agent/context_file_sources.py feeds the Rules figure; hermes prompt-size reports prompt footprint; agent/insights.py aggregates usage, cost estimates and tool/skill usage by day.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane exposes an itemised GetContextAssembly with per-segment token estimates; Hermes adds the provenance label and the 'never hide the zero row' rule for the UI.

name: Evals as release gates: behavioural harnesses beside unit tests
what: The repo ships 36 eval directories (compaction recall, tool search, delegation schema, provider fallback and wire, plugin isolation, webhook and dashboard auth, update pipeline, token accounting, prompt footprint, codebase navigability) with live A/B harnesses for context-footprint changes.
how: evals/<name>/ harnesses and READMEs; compaction evals score policies against gold questions generated from the region about to be summarised away (not token savings); tool-visibility and prefix harnesses A/B a change before it lands; plugin-isolation eval re-measures the whole catalog against HOST_UNSUPPORTED_CTX_METHODS; tests/perf_guards and fanout_resource_bench guard performance.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane's eval-lab has 14 YAML cases; the compaction-recall and tool-visibility A/B pattern is where Hermes is ahead, and the earlier Verevon docs already adopted the compaction harness.
notes: Only directory names and two READMEs were read.

name: Ink TUI as a thin renderer over a Python JSON-RPC backend
what: hermes --tui runs a Node/React (Ink fork) terminal UI that owns the screen while Python owns sessions, tools, model calls and slash logic, so TypeScript never contains agent behaviour.
how: ui-tui (React, nanostores, packages/hermes-ink fork of Ink) talks newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio to tui_gateway; key surfaces: streaming message.delta/complete, tool activity tool.start/generating/complete, approvals via server->client requests, session picker, completions through complete.slash/complete.path (which under a non-local terminal backend lists directories through the session's backend), skins delivered in gateway.ready; local built-ins (/help /quit /clear /resume /copy /paste) handled client-side, everything else slash.exec in a persistent _SlashWorker then command.dispatch.
verevonRelevance: The renderer-owns-screen/backend-owns-behaviour rule is the right split for Verevon's SolidJS UI over Model Plane SSE; completions should resolve against the session's execution environment, not the gateway host.

name: Desktop design contract: flat surfaces, one primitive per concern, intent before automation, keyboard and cancellation rules
what: A 34 KB design guide defines principles (flat not boxed, borderless floating panels, tokens over literals, one Button/Badge/SearchField/Loader/ErrorState), distinct empty/loading/reconnecting/degraded/exhausted states, direct-manipulation performance, one cancel gesture doing one thing and an i18n and checklist gate.
how: apps/desktop/DESIGN.md sections: Principles, Information architecture, Surfaces and elevation, Window glass, Stroke and colour tokens, Buttons, Badges, Profile rail, Context-sensitive dialogs, Forms, Layout, Panel titlebars, Feedback and states, Chat typography, Chat/tools/boot surfaces, Iconography, Motion, Direct manipulation and performance, Keyboard and cancellation, i18n, State, Affordances, checklist; AGENTS/ENGINEERING add: never navigate or steal focus because something happened in the background, keyboard ownership follows focus, expensive stateful surfaces (terminals) stay alive when hidden, a fast empty demo proves nothing so test against realistic transcripts; named primitives are documented with the code and a stale name is a bug.
verevonRelevance: A ready checklist for Verevon agent pages (states, cancel semantics, focus rules, i18n) that matches the 'honest states' theme in Model Plane contracts.

name: Slash palette curation authored once on the command definition
what: Each command's desktop disposition (hidden, terminal-only, messaging-only, settings-owned, advanced) is set by a desktop= field in the Python registry, while skill-derived and quick commands always remain discoverable and executable.
how: CommandDef.desktop and desktop_subcommands in hermes_cli/commands.py flow through the live commands.catalog RPC; apps/desktop/src/lib/desktop-slash-registry.json is the offline fallback regenerated by scripts/dump_desktop_slash_registry.py with drift tests on both sides; isDesktopSlashCommand gates execution, isDesktopSlashSuggestion gates discovery, isDesktopSlashExtensionCommand lets any non-built-in through; rule: curation hides noise, never user-activated extensions; only TS-only Ink commands live in a small allowlist.
verevonRelevance: Avoids the class of bug where an allow-list silently drops user commands from the palette (the stated incident), relevant when Verevon's composer starts using capability-core commands.

name: Layered i18n with plugin language packs, per-profile user overlays and surface catalogs
what: UI strings resolve plugin packs, then a user overlay in the profile, then bundled locales, then English, then the key, with 17 CLI/TUI languages and 9 desktop languages and endonyms shared with the shared TS package.
how: agent/i18n.py t(key) layers (plugin packs last-registered-wins, <home>/locales/<lang>.yaml profile-scoped, bundled locales/<lang>.yaml, the same for en, bare key), one merged dict cached per (home, lang) with reset_language_cache on pack registration or config set display.language; supported_languages() is the live union; *.tui.yaml and *.desktop.yaml pack files served through surface_catalog and the i18n.catalog RPC; plugins declare provides_locales and hermes_cli/plugin_validate_locales.py validates them; desktop overlay-completeness tests.
verevonRelevance: Verevon is Norwegian-first with refusal copy and report sections hard-coded in Rust; a layered catalogue with partial overlays would let orgs customise copy without code changes.

name: Data-driven skins and desktop themes with VS Code theme import
what: CLI skins are YAML files (colours, spinner faces and verbs, tool prefixes and emojis, branding) with inheritance from a default; desktop themes are presets plus user themes and can import VS Code themes.
how: hermes_cli/skin_engine.py SkinConfig pure data: load_skin resolves user ~/.hermes/skins/*.yaml, then built-ins (default, ares, mono, slate), missing values inherit; desktop themes/ (presets.ts, user-themes.ts, vscode.ts, accent-override.ts, chat-font.ts, install.ts, backend-sync.ts) and IPC vscode-theme/native-theme/titlebar-theme; skins arrive in gateway.ready for the TUI.
verevonRelevance: Low priority: Verevon follows Aquatiq brand rules; theme data-files matter mainly for white-label deployments.

name: Agent-asks-the-user cards: approvals, clarify, sudo and secret prompts as typed UI surfaces
what: The agent can pause to ask clarifying questions with several answers and early lock-in, request sudo or secret values through masked prompts, and request approval through a card that works on every surface.
how: server->client requests approval, clarify (answers keyed by question id, clarify.lock locks one answer early, null skips), sudo, secret, vault.code, vault.unlock_prompt rendered by ui-tui prompts.tsx / maskedPrompt.tsx and desktop gateway-event/server-requests.ts; messaging surfaces render native buttons (Telegram/Discord/Slack) with text fallback; approve/deny commands bypass both gateway message guards; plugin transports (security.approval.transport with transport_fallback: deny) can carry approvals elsewhere.
verevonRelevance: A typed question-card vocabulary (single/multi answer, masked secret, approval with scope once/session/always) is what Verevon's HITL approvals and plan-approval UI could standardise on.

name: Automation blueprints: one slot schema rendered as dashboard form, slash command and agent seed prompt
what: Recurring automations are defined once as a blueprint with typed slots (time, enum, text, weekdays); users fill a form or a pre-filled /blueprint command and never type cron.
how: cron/blueprint_catalog.py AutomationBlueprint, BlueprintSlot (types time, enum, text, weekdays), CATALOG, blueprint_form_schema, blueprint_slash_command, blueprint_deeplink, fill_blueprint validating values into cron.jobs.create_job kwargs (no second job engine); schedule_template fixes the recurrence so only human parts are slots; cron/blueprint_plugins.py lets plugins contribute.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane's scheduled runs have a cron sweeper but no authoring UX; a schema-first template that renders as form, command and agent prompt is an efficient way to ship 'daily briefing' style automations.
notes: Not in earlier Verevon docs.

name: Operator toolbox: doctor, debug dump, backup and logs with fail-closed redaction
what: hermes doctor walks a registry of checks (config drift, env, MCP security, relay plugins, certificates, gateway supervision, Python environment, tools, state, live provider probes) and --fix repairs; debug/dump bundles produce support output with strict redaction; backup/restore is SQLite-safe.
how: hermes_cli/doctor.py DOCTOR_CHECKS ordered list with Finding results and doctor_* siblings (config, connectivity, live, platform, state, tools, report primitives check_ok/warn/fail/info); doctor --live runs real-call probes with live_probe_timeout 10 s; debug_redaction.py is fail-closed redaction for text leaving support flows (secret header names, sensitive URL params compared by compact name so snake/kebab/camel match, emails); diagnostics_upload.py is opt-in; backup.py / backup_restore.py / backup_sqlite.py use SQLite-aware copies with zip packaging; hermes logs, status, insights, prompt-size.
verevonRelevance: A support/diagnostics surface Verevon lacks for self-hosted or enterprise deployments: a check registry with fix mode and a redacted support bundle.

name: Native Windows, WSL2, macOS, Linux, Termux and container support with platform-fact resolvers
what: Hermes installs natively on Windows 10/11 (no WSL), on WSL2, macOS and Linux, on Android via Termux (APT repo for aarch64 with stable and canary channels) and as a container, with Windows-specific handling for shells, PTY, scheduled-task gateway services and App Installer updates.
how: hermes_platform/host answers OS family, native architecture (IsWow64Process2 not PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE alone), CPU identity and WSL/container/Termux with facts cached per process and no environment-variable input (so a hardware recogniser cannot be set from a shell); hermes_platform/resolver is the only place for executable and known-dir lookup (a bare shutil.which outside fails a test unless allowlisted); install.ps1 to %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes; gateway as a Scheduled Task; pywinpty and pywin32 dependencies; scripts/termux builds CPython, node, uv and wheels for Termux with deb/APT staging; CI jobs for install E2E on Linux, macOS and Windows and wine2e markers.
verevonRelevance: Matters only if Verevon ships a local connector or desktop agent; Windows-native without WSL is a real requirement for the Aquatiq user base (Windows 11).

name: Cron and automation delivery surfaces: send CLI, webhooks and home-channel routing
what: Scripts can pipe output into any connected platform with hermes send, cron results are delivered to a home channel or explicit target (platform:chat_id), and inbound webhooks start agent turns with coalescing and filters.
how: gateway/delivery.py (direct reply, home channel, explicit target, cross-platform delivery), hermes send CLI and a send_message tool, gateway/platforms/webhook.py with webhook_coalesce.py and webhook_filters.py, msgraph_webhook.py for Microsoft Graph change notifications, cron deliver: targets, hermes webhook subcommand and desktop /webhooks page; webhook sessions run under the unattended approval mode and the safe toolset.
verevonRelevance: A Teams/Outlook change-notification webhook that starts a governed agent turn fits the Microsoft-heavy Aquatiq stack; Hermes shows the coalescing/filter layer needed to avoid event storms.

name: Dependency-light stdlib transports and lazy imports to keep startup cheap
what: Heavy SDKs (messaging platforms, MCP, websockets, OpenTelemetry) are imported only when used, and many internal packages export names lazily so import cycles and cold-start costs stay low.
how: Deferred platform loaders (register_deferred) in gateway/platform_registry.py, PEP 562 lazy exports in tools/connectors/__init__.py and hermes_cli/local_runtime/__init__.py (documented reason: eager imports deadlocked the concurrent registry scan and updaters that import the NEW checkout under OLD modules), websockets imported only once a CDP supervisor connects (~22 ms), A2A plugin uses stdlib http.server/urllib, AST discovery cache for tools, models.dev stale-while-revalidate; HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS switch for lazy pip installs.
verevonRelevance: Cold start is mostly a Python concern; the transferable point is that cross-version updater/old-module hazards justify lazy exports in any plugin-hosting runtime.
